narrative:
The model estimates a 55% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall career experience of just 1-5 years was the strongest influence pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expects to stay, only about half have similarly limited experience, while many others bring 6 or more years. This shorter track record makes the model see higher turnover risk.

The fact that you have received other job offers while working here was the second most important factor, pushing the prediction toward leaving. Most employees the model predicts will stay (77%) have not received outside opportunities, so your access to alternatives signals you may be more likely to depart.

Your employment in the “other” sector, rather than medical or education, was the third notable influence and also nudged the outcome toward leaving. This sector shows a somewhat different pattern of retention compared with the larger fields where most stayers work.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive signals such as your satisfaction with the job itself and the training you found useful. The organization should consider discussing your career development goals with you and exploring whether additional responsibilities or clearer advancement paths could strengthen your connection to the company. You may also want to reflect on how the external opportunities align with your long-term plans.
